lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: Honey, if it has wheels I can talk about it all day. If it hasn't, see my clerk.

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: Well now. Owen Pritchard's sent me a gun with legs. Sit. Four trains in a month, honey, and a hymn chalked on every boiler. Tonight I send the payroll and the fever physic through Sawtooth Cut. I want you on the footplate.

buttons.label: Who passes your trains as sound?

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: So you're the one sent Pritchard a page of my Line 14. I've had the inspector's desk nailed shut since, and no, you may not see in it. Sit down anyway. I need a gun more than I need to like you.

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: Silas Vane wrote me. A certain book has come into his keeping, he says, and no inquiry need ever trouble me. Now who sold him that, I wonder. Sit down, honey. Let's see what else you'll do for money.

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: Preacher Dole. He lifts a rail, lets the Lord and the grade do the rest, and holds a service on what's left. Thirty rifles say amen. I'd admire to see him answer for it. I'd admire it more to see my mail get through.

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: Every car on this line is passed by the Inspector of Way, and stamped. You want to read stamps, read stamps. The train leaves at dark whether you can read or not.

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: Billie drives. Do what she says about the engine and nothing she says about anything else. And honey? If it comes down to the mail or the girl, you bring me the girl.

lines.speaker: tarrow
lines.text: If it's about the brakes, I know. If it's about a bet, I'm listening.

lines.speaker: tarrow
lines.text: You're the gun? You don't look like much. Neither does she. Old Contrary: eleven tons, nine of them spite. Hold that. Not that, that comes off. Bet you a day's pay you're sick before the Cut.

lines.speaker: tarrow
lines.text: Rail's spread on the left hand, about so much. Not gone. Spread. Anything heavy lies down on its side. Anything light, going like the devil had a mortgage on it... well. Nobody's tried. Don't tell Gussie I said that.

lines.speaker: tarrow
lines.text: Lanterns. That's him. That's all of them. Rail's out just where I said. I can stop her, I can back her, or I can find out something nobody knows about this engine. Your gun, your say. QUICK.

lines.speaker: dole
lines.text: The service is at dusk, traveller, wherever the rail gives out. All are welcome. Most arrive suddenly.

lines.speaker: dole
lines.text: Evening, traveller. The text tonight is four foot eight and one half. I measured this rail nineteen years, and they signed my name to it after I was in the ground. Step down off her lie and hear the rest.

buttons.label: They buried you. Who are you?

lines.speaker: dole
lines.text: Ostrander. Inspector of Way. I condemned the Greenwater trestle and they ran a train over it that same week. Then the fever, and a pest-house, and a hymn. Somebody in that yard still stamps my name on scrap iron. Ask who.

buttons.label: And the silver in your plate?

lines.speaker: dole
lines.text: Comes by a man who comes by a man. A square mark on every piece. It buys powder. I'd lift these rails for love, traveller. I take the silver so the Lord is not left out of pocket.

lines.speaker: dole
lines.text: A third of the pay-chest, and the girl walks home unharmed. The physic goes up the hill: my people have the fever too, and nobody ever sent them a train. Say done and step off the footplate.

lines.speaker: dole
lines.text: Then here endeth the lesson. I will count three for you, which is three more than the yard gave anybody on the morning train. One.

lines.speaker: tarrow
lines.text: HA! Did you... we were in the AIR! She's bent, she's a little bit on fire, I think I bit my tongue through. You owe me a day's pay. No. I owe you. Oh, Gussie's going to skin me.

lines.speaker: tarrow
lines.text: Well. Nobody's dead. That's the best I can say for it. You want to tell her, or shall I? ...I'll tell her. You'd only make it sound sensible.

lines.speaker: tarrow
lines.text: Don't. Don't say one word to me. It's eleven miles and I know every tie. There are children in that valley with the fever and I was going to drive it to them. You think of that when you spend it.

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: You jumped my engine over a hole. She's a wreck. The physic's in the valley and the payroll's in my safe and I have not been this happy since I was a bride. Ask me for something.

buttons.label: Whose hand is on your inspections?

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: Dole's dead? ...You'll think me foolish. Six years back I read at a funeral for a man who used to stand right where you are and tell me no. I'd have liked to hear no again. Well. The line's open.

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: Billie walked in at four this morning. Eleven miles. She told me what you did, and then she asked me not to have you shot. So I'm asking you nicely, honey. Get out of my yard.

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: That's his hand. That's Reuben's own hand. He's ALIVE? ...Top drawer, honey. Go on. You'd find it anyway. Nobody would come out to inspect a line that kills inspectors. So Reuben went on inspecting.

lines.speaker: lockridge
lines.text: Every stamp was a train that ran. Physic, seed corn, coal. I never did the other sum and I'll thank you not to do it for me. Well? You've the drawer open. What becomes of an old woman and a dead man's name?

buttons.label: Keep stamping. Trains have to run.
Sign your own name from now on.
